weight-perception-based novel control can be used to enhance performances of a power-assist robot for cooperative lifting of light-weight objects.

weight perception due the inertia of a power assist robot can be different from that by gravity when lifting an objects with power assist and that the novel control based on human features can reduce load forces and accelerates and improve performances in terms of safety and maneuverability.

weight perception due the inertia of the object being lifted with a power assist robot differs from that due to the gravity of the object being handled by a human and that a novel control that reduces excessive load forces and excessive accelerations may enhance performances in terms of safety, maneuverability etc.

the development of a novel control based upon human features to enhance the performances of power-assist robots.

the development of power-assist robots for the cooperative lifting of light-weight objects.
